user.title: Compute Blade Fan
user.description: Counts the fan's tach pulses on a GPIO and reads the duty the kernel pwm-fan driver applies. The defaults suit a Compute Blade (CM5) with the fan unit on header J1.

data_description.gpio_chip_label: pinctrl-rp1 on a Raspberry Pi 5 / CM5.
data_description.pulses_per_rev: 2 for Noctua and most PC fans.
data_description.stall_seconds: How long the fan may report no pulses while it should be spinning.

error.chip_not_found: No GPIO chip with that label. Is Home Assistant running on the Raspberry Pi?
error.line_busy: That GPIO is in use by something else (another integration or an add-on).
error.invalid_gpio: That GPIO doesn't exist on this chip.

abort.already_configured: This tach GPIO is already configured.

pwm_fan_missing.title: Fan isn't under kernel control
pwm_fan_missing.description: No pwm-fan device was found, so the fan isn't following the CPU temperature, and duty and stall detection are unavailable. Add the pwm-fan overlay to config.txt on the boot partition (see the documentation) and reboot the host.
